subject: Annotating a plot without explicit indication of position

messages.author: 0600694caf57b8fb
messages.subject: Annotating a plot without explicit indication of position
parts:
Hi all,

in the below example I have 2 distribution the mean of which I want to
write in the plot using geom_text.

I know I can create a dataframe indicating the positions where I want
the means to be plotted but is there a way to just indicate that I
want the text to be plotted let's say in the top-left corner without
specifying each position?

Sometimes what I do is just indicate one position and use jitter to
avoid overploting like in the example below but the problem is that
everything is misaligned. Thanks.

library("ggplot2")
library("plyr")
n=1000
df1<-data.frame(resp=rnorm(n,0,10),distribution="a")
df2<-data.frame(resp=rnorm(n,2,5),distribution="b")
df<-rbind(df1,df2)

compute.mean<-function(x) data.frame(mean=mean(x$resp))
means<-ddply(df,.(distribution),compute.mean)

p<-ggplot()
p<-p+ geom_freqpoly(data=df,aes
(x=resp,y=..density..,color=distribution),binwidth = 1)
p<-p+ geom_text(data=means,aes(x=-20,y=0.08,label=paste("mean:
",mean),color=distribution),
legend=F,position=position_jitter(height=0.02))
p<-p+ xlim(-30,30)
p


ps: does someone know why the y-label shows '0.08' instead of
'density'?

messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: Re: Annotating a plot without explicit indication of position
parts:
p <- p + xlim(-30,30)

# one solution:
p + annotate("text",x=-30,y=0.06,label=paste("mean:",means$mean,
collapse="\n"), hjust=0, vjust=0)
# NB: setting hjust and vjust this way sets the lower left corner of
the text to (x,y), which is easier to deal with that the default (text
centered)

> ps: does someone know why the y-label shows '0.08' instead of
> 'density'?

because you specified y=0.08 *inside* the aes call. So it maps the
variable "0,08" to y. Such scalar values need to be set as parameters,
not aesthetics = outside the aes call.

Now the remaining issue would be to map the color of the text to the
color of the curves. There are two solutions:
- using scale_colour_manual for the freqpoly and setting manually the
same colors in two annotate calls
- use a geom_text to draw the text but either this way:
p + geom_text(data=means, mapping=aes(colour=distribution,
label=paste("mean:", mean)),x=-30,y=0.06, hjust=0, vjust=0)
i.e. with x and y outside the aes call, or by adding the coordinates
in two columns resp and density in the dataframe means, and mapping
those inside the aes call:
means$resp=-30
means$density=c(0.06, 0.07)
p + geom_text(data=means, mapping=aes(x=resp, y=density,
colour=distribution, label=paste("mean:", mean)), hjust=0, vjust=0)

I hope that helps.

JiHO
